blocks.content: The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the land, establishing the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions.

items: Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) was described as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
The Right to Property was removed from Fundamental Rights and made a legal right under Article 300A by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 is frequently referred to in competitive exams as the 'Mini-Constitution' due to its comprehensive changes.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into force on 26th January 1950.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly.
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 introduced key terms including 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' into the Preamble.
Fundamental Rights are legally enforceable in court, whereas Directive Principles of State Policy serve as non-justiciable guidelines.
